failures.criterion: Outcome: an event reaches the session once, also when published while it was down, as long as the session comes back under the same session id; a message the plugin cannot inject is not silently dropped
failures.evidence: A card handed to omp while a turn is streaming is held in omp's memory (deliverAs steer) and written to the session file only when the turn takes it, but the plugin records it shown at once (envoy-replay-delivered entry, and the replay-state cursor moves past it). If the process ends before the turn takes it, the message is lost for good: the resumed session's ledger says shown and its cursor is past it. Live run r2 (real omp, natsd -js, listener from this head; https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/2228#issuecomment-6408420209): live frames 801..805 published while isStreaming=true -> card=0, ledger=Y; SIGKILL; after resume + 4 heartbeats card=0 for all five. Same for 811..815 stored while the connection was down and replayed mid-turn. Leg D: a sweep replayed 40 stored frames, the first card started a turn, SIGKILL 1.5 s later -> 2 cards in the file, 40 ledger entries, cursor 85; after resume the other 38 never showed. An rpc abort instead of a kill does not lose them (821..825 all shown). Red tests (commit 'test(pi-envoy): a card omp still held queued when the process ended is shown again after the restart (red)'): `cd packages/pi-envoy && bun test extensions/envoy.test.ts -t "a card the host had not written"` -> 2 fail, each at the held card (expected 1, received 0) while the written sibling stays 0. The fix must tie 'shown' (ledger and cursor) to the card reaching the transcript; the existing test 'a frame delivered live is not shown again when the same envelope arrives after a restart' restores entries without the card's custom_message entry, so it will need that entry once 'shown' is read from the transcript.

observations: /v1/replay trusts a self-asserted session_id, as every /v1 route does: a caller with the listener's access can read 72 h of any listed session's stored agent subject by naming its id. Sessions could already subscribe to notifications.> live; this adds stored history. Not recorded as a failure under the deployment's trust model; the reviewer may judge it.

After /new, the issue topics the previous session followed stay subscribed and get cursors in the new session (pre-existing subscription carry-over; the old session's agent-subject frame stayed out of the new transcript and showed once on switching back).
